note: 5 EPOCH(S), --rank-form rel at --alpha-rank 75 plus the PAE term, FULLY UNCROPPED, over 849 of 853 declared, less 5 skipped: 4zto,9dzf,9dzg,9mx1,9q5m. 6,903 units in 230 cross-seed steps of 30. THE EXCLUSION IS NOW MEASURED, NOT PREDICTED. peak_GB = 2.02 + 2.896e-05 * tokens^2 was fitted on the FULL-BACKWARD arm (tvqobh) and does not transfer to the frozen graph: it put 2,289 tokens at 154 GB, and the frozen graph peaks at 60. Measured on one card, checkpointing OFF, expandable_segments, full pass A and pass B: 1,650 tok (4rdq) peak 54.57 GB, 1,822 (9q5v) 66.15 GB, 2,004 (7m7i) 79.64 GB -- all fitting on a 94.97 GB card -- and 2,289 (9dzf/9dzg) OOM, short by about 10 GB. So the cut is between 2,004 and 2,289 and only 9dzf/9dzg are excluded. CAVEAT ON THAT: those are SINGLE-RANK, 2-seed probes. The arm runs 3 ranks over 30-unit steps with the prefix cache live, and tztukd and kfthfe both died at step 158 rather than step 1, so the failure mode is STEP COMPOSITION rather than single-pose capacity. 2,004 tokens at 79.64 GB is 84% of the card. This is what killed tztukd and kfthfe at the same step 158 under thresholds 855 and 0 -- the threshold was never the cause. THE RANKS ARE NOW BALANCED: a step is dealt round-robin across its structures via lr_schedule.deal_round_robin instead of shuffled globally, so each rank gets 5 seeds of each of the step's 2 structures rather than a random 10 of 30. Per-step tokens^2 imbalance falls from a median of 17.2% to 0.0% (90 of 230 steps over 20% to 13, those 13 being the all-shallow steps where no assignment can balance). --ckpt-token-threshold 855 turns checkpointing OFF at or below 855 tokens; 855 was measured on a population under token dropout where it meant ~427 effective tokens, so --mem-log is ON to read the unchecked peaks rather than assume them. rel regresses on the true iTM after mean-centring, so it uses every pose of an interface regardless of seed and has no pair family or tau. INSTRUMENTATION: --mem-log prints allocated/peak/reserved per pose with the token count and the pass, which is how the n^2 fit above was obtained and how the 855 threshold's unchecked peaks are being checked. It costs a print per pose. NOTE the lines carry NO RANK LABEL, so three ranks interleave in one log -- read them as a population, not a sequence. --trunk-memmap maps z_trunk out of the npz in place instead of reading it into a heap buffer; gated bit-identical on CPU, so it changes epoch time and nothing else. --trunk-cache-gb 10 holds a step's uncropped trunks as host numpy arrays so pass A and pass B read each unit once instead of twice, warmed on the prefetch workers. It changes epoch time and nothing else. IN-BLOCK POSE INJECTION: the pose enters pairformer block 3 AFTER tri_mul_in and BEFORE tri_att_start, with both the 39-bin one-hot distance term and the raw-distance term, and again after pae_ln in the PAE readout. Blocks 0-2 and block 3's tri_mul_out/tri_mul_in are FROZEN via --train-only 'pairformer_stack\.blocks\.3\.tri_att_start\.,pairformer_stack\.blocks\.3\.pair_transition\.,^pose_inblock_,^linear_no_bias_pae\.,^pae_ln\.'; trainable is block 3's tri_att_start, tri_att_end and pair_transition plus the injections and the PAE readout. THE PLACEMENT IS THE POINT: autograd starts at the first op whose parameters or inputs require grad, so injecting at the block INPUT -- where --pose-perblock injects -- would put both frozen tri-muls back into the backward and lose the saving silently; run_logging/test_pose_inblock_graph.py asserts the boundary with a negative control that reproduces exactly that failure. Both injections are ZERO-INIT and verified exactly zero, so step 0 is bit-identical to the un-injected head. THIS IS A CAPACITY CHANGE ON TOP OF A FREEZE AND A DIFFERENT ARM -- it is NOT comparable against mqird6 and needs its own held-out control. The readout injection is added AFTER the layer norm, so an unnormalised quantity is added to a normalised one and nothing downstream rescales it. UNTESTED on a GPU. EXTRA ARGS: --skip-dead-ops --lr-steps 20:1e-3,40:1e-4 --eval-pool-every 5 --prefix-cache-gb 10.
